title: fix(fields): the position-ref grant picker stops offering the audience anchors (objectui#12200)
body:
Fixes #12200
Clause-②: no

The `position-ref` grant picker (`@object-ui/fields`, `RegistryRefField`) stops offering the `everyone` and `guest` audience anchors. A grant cannot name one: every authenticated or anonymous principal holds an anchor implicitly (ADR-0090 D5/D9), and the server refuses a `sys_user_position` row that names one. The on-record measurement is objectstack-ai/objectstack#22967's browser check (comment 6120504736): 16 positions listed, `everyone` among them.

## What changes

- `position-ref` leaves out exactly the spec's `AUDIENCE_ANCHOR_POSITIONS`, read from `@objectstack/spec` and never copied, so an anchor the spec adds is left out with no change here.
- A row that already stores an anchor still shows it, by its label beside its name, as its own option. It is not flagged "not found", because the registry does list it. When the row holds another value, no anchor is offered. Read-only shows the same label.
- A registry that lists nothing but anchors gives the typed-name box, the LOADED-but-empty arm, now judged on what a grant can name.
- `permission-ref` is unchanged: a permission set named like an anchor is listed and written as before.
- There is no new prop, widget option, type member or i18n string. There is one `@object-ui/fields` patch changeset.

## H1: the mark, measured

- `@objectstack/spec` exports `AUDIENCE_ANCHOR_POSITIONS` from both its root entry and `./identity`. The declaration is `declare const AUDIENCE_ANCHOR_POSITIONS: readonly ["everyone", "guest"];`.
- `@object-ui/fields` declares `^17.6.0`; the lockfile installs **17.7.0**. The 17.7.0 `dist/identity/index.d.ts` re-exports it (`b as AUDIENCE_ANCHOR_POSITIONS`). A runtime import of `@objectstack/spec/identity` answers `["everyone","guest"]`.
- The range floor, the **17.6.0** registry tarball, exports it from `dist/index.d.mts` and `dist/identity/index.d.ts` too.
- The registry marks no item itself. `PositionSchema` has no anchor key, and the meta read gives `{ name, label }` headers. The spec constant IS the mark, so no name is hard-coded here and no server-side companion is owed.
- On the server, the grant refusal is `plugin-security`'s `delegated-admin-gate.ts` invariant ("audience anchor is implicit — it cannot be assigned via sys_user_position"), on objectstack `main` and on objectstack-ai/objectstack#22939's head. That gate keeps its own `new Set(['everyone', 'guest'])` and does not import the constant (see Acceptance notes). The catalog-activation gate in `packages/runtime` does import it.

## H2: which import, measured three ways

`RegistryRefField.tsx` IS in the console's eager closure. The console's chunk grouping puts `packages/fields` into the eager `ui-components` chunk (the gate's chunk-membership line), and the widget's own string `fields.registryRef.loadFailed` sits in `ui-components-*.js`, which `eager-closure.json` lists. `@objectstack/spec/identity` is a lazy chunk of its own (`identity-*.js`, not in the eager list).

| route | eager closure, gzip bytes vs base | `ui-components` vs its ceiling | `check:eager-closure` | `check:spec-floors`, `@object-ui/fields` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `9646e2e` | | 281.5 KB / 282.2 KB | exit 0 | not built |
| static `import … from '@objectstack/spec/identity'` (counterfactual, restored) | +6953 | 288.3 KB, over by 6.1 KB | exit 1 | not run |
| lazy `import('@objectstack/spec/identity')` (commit `8bd8a14`) | +174 | 281.7 KB | exit 0 | `opaque-subpath` finding, exit 1 |
| static import from the root `@objectstack/spec` (this PR, `aa16a9c`) | −5 (noise) | 281.6 KB | exit 0 | judged clean (308 pairs judged, against 307 for the lazy build) |

Why `check:spec-floors` decides it: `changeset:publish` runs `scripts/check-spec-range-floors.mjs` before `changeset publish`, and so does the nightly `spec-range-floors.yml`. The gate reads symbol names from static imports only. A dynamic `import()` leaves the subpath unjudged, and the gate reports that as a finding, so the lazy route would have reddened the publish lane.

So the PR takes a third route that the dispatch's static-or-lazy framing did not name. It imports statically from the root entry, as `@object-ui/auth` imports `BUILTIN_MEMBERSHIP_ROLES`. It keeps the suggested shape: a `Set` built from `AUDIENCE_ANCHOR_POSITIONS`, keyed on `registryType === 'position'`, one small helper (`nonGrantableNames`) beside the widget. The anchor set is known on the first render, so no catalog arm changes shape. Commit `aa16a9c` says why the lazy commit was replaced.

## H3: every `position-ref` field

- objectstack `main` `6a40a09ed`: none. `git grep -c position-ref` answers 0; the control, `widget: '…-ref'` on the same tree, finds two `object-ref` declarations.
- objectstack-ai/objectstack#22939 head `7de0f00c9`: exactly one, **`sys_user_position.position`** (`plugin-security`, `sys-user-position.object.ts`), beside `permission-ref` on `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set`. The server refuses an anchor there, so no field declares `position-ref` where an anchor is a valid value.
- objectui: no object field declares it; only the docs examples do.

## Tests, at `aa16a9c`

- New `RegistryRefField.audienceAnchors-12200.test.tsx` has 5 pins: the anchors are left out, an anchors-only registry gives the text box, a stored `everyone` shows unflagged as its own option (H4), a read-only stored anchor shows its label, and `permission-ref` lists and writes a set named `everyone` (H5).
- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the six files that render the widget, run as one command: `Test Files 6 passed (6)`, `Tests 311 passed (311)`. The files are the two `RegistryRefField` suites, `widget-aria-invalid-registry-e2e`, `widget-dom-leak-e2e`, `plugin-form`'s `objectFormRegistryNameWidget-7611` and `components`' `form-data-source-wiring`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` exits 0. `tsconfig.test.json` lists the new test file.
- Reverse verification ran on the committed fix. Each mutation went through `ablation-replace.mjs`, and each restore was proven by blob == HEAD with an empty `git diff HEAD`:
  - the filter off: 3 failed / 12 passed;
  - the stored anchor's own option off: 1 failed / 14 passed;
  - a partial list (`[AUDIENCE_ANCHOR_POSITIONS[0]]`): 3 failed / 12 passed.
- Gates, run after the last commit: `check:eager-closure` 0, `check:phantom-deps` 0, `check:vi-mock-specifiers` 0, `check:vi-mock-inherit` 0, `check:vi-mock-override-shape` 0, `check:spec-symbols` 0, `check:esm-specifiers` 0, `check-changeset-presence.mjs` 0, `check:changeset-claims` 0, `check:pending-changeset-literals` 0, `check:control-bytes` 0, `check:new-line-citations` 0.
- `check:spec-floors` exits 1 locally, and every one of its 15 findings is `no-artifact` for a package this tree did not build. `@object-ui/fields` was built and has no finding. A Node ESM import of the built `@object-ui/fields` dist loads.
- ESLint over the two changed sources: 2 files, 0 errors, 2 `no-explicit-any` warnings (test casts, as in the 7611 suite). Type-aware linting is not configured, so the result for untouched files cannot move.

## Acceptance notes

- **Docs.** `content/docs/guide/fields.md` and `packages/fields/README.md` describe `position-ref` as listing "the `position` registry" and do not mention the exclusion. They are outside this claim's file surface; one sentence in each would cover it.
- **The server keeps a second copy of the list.** `delegated-admin-gate.ts`'s `ANCHOR_POSITIONS` is a literal `['everyone', 'guest']`, not the spec constant. The values agree today. Noted, not filed.
- **`check:spec-floors` reads no dynamic `import()`.** A symbol taken that way is never judged against the floor. app-shell's lazy `/identity` imports (`audienceAnchorsOf`, `clientValidation`) pass only because `FlowReferenceField.tsx` imports that subpath statically. Noted, not filed.
- **Headroom.** `ui-components` has 0.7 KB of per-chunk headroom before and after this PR. The next growth of `@object-ui/fields` meets that ceiling.
- **Browser.** No re-check was run after this change; it needs objectstack-ai/objectstack#22939's server.

Dev run for objectui#12200, seat `domain:ui#1`, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_016djJF12Qt14ejKR5Vjt4sK`.
